metadataReview.note: Reviewed location: Appian (Civil Wars 1.116) states that Spartacus and his companions took refuge on Mount Vesuvius and that the first forces sent against them were beaten; Plutarch (Crassus 9) describes the Roman siege of their hill, with a single narrow ascent, and the descent by vine ladders that routed the besiegers. Frontinus (Strategemata I.5.21) names the place: Spartacus was 'besieged on the slopes of Vesuvius' by Clodius and escaped down the steepest, unguarded side. The cited Wikipedia revision places this siege on Mount Vesuvius. The point is the gazetteer position of the Vesuvius summit, used as a mountain reference. The existing year (-72, i.e. 73 BC in astronomical numbering) is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: GeoNames 3164481, Vesuvius (feature class volcano, elevation 1281 m, Ottaviano, Province of Naples), publishes latitude 40.82261 and longitude 14.4292; OSM peak node 12995577013 (Vesuvio) coincides. Stored as [14.4292,40.8226]. This is a mountain reference for the named site, not the rebels' camp, the single ascent held by the Romans, the cliff face they descended or the Roman camp; the ancient sources do not locate any of these on the mountain. The present-day summit is used only as the gazetteer anchor of the named mountain. No positional accuracy radius is claimed.
